audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers rendered different level charts: every phases[N].side read 'Skill' while win[] read Aurelion Sol / Skill / Skill / Aurelion Sol / Vladimir / Aurelion Sol / Aurelion Sol.
audit.why: The content-layer chart matches packet.levelChart and the 49.51% winrate over 814 games. Vladimir has no level-1 kill pressure, the lane flattens 2-3, and level 6 is his one clear window because Sanguine Pool's 2 untargetable seconds dodge Falling Star.
audit.corrected: Adopt the content chart and flip phases[0], [3], [4], [5], [6].side to match, proposed as an atomic group with the win[] rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes and prose referenced 'Starsurge' and 'Comet of Legend' — neither is an Aurelion Sol ability.
audit.why: His kit is Breath of Light (Q), Astral Flight (W), Singularity/black hole (E) and Falling Star, which upgrades into The Skies Descend once enough Stardust is banked.
audit.corrected: All references rewritten to the real abilities and to Stardust as the scaling resource.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither the untargetability window nor the anti-heal requirement was stated with real numbers, and Tides of Blood's minion-block was absent entirely.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16s for 2 seconds of untargetable, which dodges Falling Star's stun and the black hole's execute outright. Transfusion is free-cost and near-spammable and Hemoplague heals per champion hit, so Grievous Wounds timing decides every extended trade. Riot's own text says Tides of Blood 'can be blocked by enemy units', so standing behind your wave denies it.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.cooldowns, whys[4], spikes[1], mid and dontsFull[0].

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Astral Flight has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1, still 16s maxed, two untargetable seconds — count it out, then spend Falling Star. - Tides of Blood is blocked by minions: stand behind your wave. - Transfusion costs him nothing, so anti-heal it rather than out-chipping it.

edits.after: Carry by scaling honestly — Stardust is permanent, and Vladimir's HP-ratio damage caps out where your Breath of Light simply does not.

edits.before: Ahead, compound it: shove with E executes, burn Vladimir on every W rotation, and group early — your beam turns small mid-game leads into unanswerable objective control.
edits.after: Ahead, deny the stack: shove with E, then W over the wall and burn him off the side wave — a Vladimir with no CS is a health bar with no damage, and anti-heal keeps him there.

edits.after: Vladimir wins by pooling out of your commit, healing it straight back, and Hemoplague-amplifying the fight he chose.

edits.before: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Every second of beam on him is permanent Stardust — bait Sanguine Pool first, or two seconds erase your commit.

edits.before: That is Vladimir’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.

notes: Fabricated names killed: 'Starsurge' and 'Comet of Legend' are not Aurelion Sol abilities in the current kit; replaced with Falling Star / The Skies Descend / Stardust. The full and content layers shipped two different level charts here (all-Skill vs the packet chart) — proposed as matched pairs on the content-layer version. Tides of Blood's minion block is taken from Riot's own description ('can be blocked by enemy units'), not from a derived flag.
